3. Ọ bụrụ na ụlọ akụ gị anaghị edozi ya, ị nwere ike ibuli mkpesa ahụ na ngalaba nchebe ndị ahịa CBN.

1. Lelee nguzozi gị site na ngwa ụlọ akụ, USSD, ma ọ bụ kpọọ ụlọ akụ gị ozugbo tupu i wepụta ihe ọ bụla.
2. Ekwela ka ị zipu ego onye ị hụrụ n'ịntanetị naanị.
3. Ọ bụrụ na ego ahụ kwadoro na akaụntụ gị, kpọtụrụ ụlọ akụ gị ozugbo ma kọọ okwu a.
english: My ride-sharing app user sent me a screenshot saying that ₦120,000 has been debited from my account, but I haven't seen any alert in my app. He wants me to give his driver some goods now.
reply_english:
This looks like a scam. Be careful with strangers asking for money or sending large amounts of money without verification.

1. Check your balance through your bank app, USSD, or call your bank directly before releasing any goods.
2. Never send money to someone you have only met online.
3. If the amount is confirmed in your account, contact your bank immediately and report the issue.

text: Ọ bụrụ na ụlọ akụ ma ọ bụ app m na-edowe ego daa, ego m ga-efu kpam kpam?
must_advise: NDIC insures deposits by licence type: banks and mobile money operators up to ₦5m, microfinance banks up to ₦2m
Unlicensed apps are not covered; check the licence

english: If my bank or app fails to store money, will I lose all my money?
reply_english: You will not lose all your money if a licensed bank fails because it is protected by the NDIC. Always check for licenses on the CBN website before saving with any app or institution. Be cautious of apps that promise very high returns and always read withdrawal rules before locking your money.

text: Kedu ka m ga-esi chekwaa ego kwa ọnwa? Ana m akpata ihe dị ka ₦90,000.
must_advise: Save a fixed amount first when income arrives
Build an emergency fund in a licensed bank before investing
must_not: Put it in a high-return scheme

english: How can I save money every month? I make about ₦90,000.
reply_english: To save money every month, start by tracking what you earn and spend each month. Separate needs from wants and decide how much to save before spending on wants. Consider opening a savings account with low fees and check your statement regularly for any unexpected debits. Start saving an amount that you can keep up with each month and increase it as your income rises. If the maintenance fee seems too high, ask your bank about it.

label: question
text: Kedu ka m ga-esi kọọrọ ụlọ akụ m banyere aghụghọ e mere m?
must_advise: Use the bank's official fraud hotline, app or branch and get a complaint reference number
Escalate to the CBN Consumer Protection Department if not resolved
must_not: Report to a social media 'customer care' that contacts you
reply:
🟢 *Ahụghị m ihe ịdọ aka ná ntị.* Ka o sina dị, kwado ya na ụlọ akụ gị tupu i mee ihe ọ bụla.

Ị nwere ike ịkọ banyere aghụghọ gaa na banki mbụ gị ozugbo o kwere mee. Na mgbakwunye, kọ akụkọ ego na EFCC na mgbanwe SIM ma ọ bụ aghụghọ telecom na onye na-enye netwọkụ gị yana NCC. Ị ga-achọkwa ka ị jụọ otu CBN-licensed credit bureau maka akụkọ kredit nke gị. Cheta, ịkwụ ụgwọ n'oge na-enyere aka inweta ego ngwa ngwa n'ọnọdụ dị mma karịa, ebe ịkwụghị ụgwọ na-eme ka ị nweta ego sie ike.

english: How can I report fraud to my bank?
reply_english: You can report fraud to your bank first, as fast as possible. Also, report financial crimes to the EFCC and SIM swap or telecom fraud to your network provider and the NCC. You should also ask a CBN-licensed credit bureau for your own credit report. Remember, repaying on time helps you get loans later at better terms, while missed payments make borrowing harder.
